title: Non-Hermitian dynamics in a driven-dissipative and spatially correlated light-matter system
summary: Pure quantum states, as described in quantum mechanics textbooks, are ideal representations inevitably deteriorated in real systems by any dissipative connection to the environment. In this work we derive a unified theoretical frame to study the non-Hermitian dynamics of a driven-dissipative quantum system and validate it by comparison to experimental data of matter-wave diffraction. To highlight the role of dissipation, we perform the comparison in a near-resonant regime of light-matter interaction, where perturbative approaches fail.
